claim: Tissue mechanics is important for development.
source: Tissue mechanics is important for development
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific supporting data in the manuscript.

claim: The spatio-temporal dynamics of in vivo tissue stiffness is still poorly understood.
source: the spatio-temporal dynamics of in vivo tissue stiffness is still poorly understood
evidence: This is presented as a knowledge gap motivating the study.

claim: The authors developed tiv-AFM, combining time-lapse in vivo atomic force microscopy with upright fluorescence imaging of embryonic tissue.
source: We here developed tiv-AFM, combining time-lapse in vivo atomic force microscopy with upright fluorescence imaging of embryonic tissue
evidence: This is a methodological claim describing the technique developed by the authors.

claim: During development, local tissue stiffness changes significantly within tens of minutes.
source: during development local tissue stiffness changes significantly within tens of minutes
evidence: This is a primary finding from the tiv-AFM measurements described in the abstract.

claim: A stiffness gradient arose in the developing Xenopus brain within tens of minutes.
source: Within this time frame, a stiffness gradient arose in the developing Xenopus brain
evidence: This is a specific finding from the tiv-AFM experiments on Xenopus embryos.

claim: Retinal ganglion cell axons turned to follow the stiffness gradient.
source: retinal ganglion cell axons turned to follow this gradient
evidence: This describes the observed behavior of axons in relation to the measured stiffness gradient.

claim: Changes in local tissue stiffness were largely governed by cell proliferation.
source: Changes in local tissue stiffness were largely governed by cell proliferation
evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion based on perturbation experiments described in the abstract.

claim: Perturbation of mitosis diminished the stiffness gradient in developing brains.
source: perturbation of mitosis diminished both the stiffness gradient
evidence: This describes the effect of mitosis perturbation on tissue stiffness gradients.

claim: Perturbation of mitosis diminished the caudal turn of axons found in control brains.
source: perturbation of mitosis diminished both the stiffness gradient and the caudal turn of axons found in control brains
evidence: This describes the effect of mitosis perturbation on axon guidance.

claim: There is a close relationship between the dynamics of tissue mechanics and developmental processes.
source: we identified a close relationship between the dynamics of tissue mechanics and developmental processes
evidence: This is a general conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Time-resolved stiffness measurements are important for understanding developmental processes.
source: underpinning the importance of time-resolved stiffness measurements
evidence: This is an implication drawn from the findings about rapid stiffness changes.

claim: All animal experiments were approved by the Ethical Review Committee of the University of Cambridge.
source: All animal experiments were approved by the Ethical Review Committee of the University of Cambridge
evidence: This is a statement of ethical compliance.

claim: All animal experiments complied with guidelines set by the UK Home Office.
source: complied with guidelines set by the UK Home Office
evidence: This is a statement of regulatory compliance.

claim: Single-cell-stage, wild-type Xenopus laevis embryos of both sexes were obtained via in vitro fertilisation.
source: Single-cell-stage, wild-type Xenopus laevis embryos of both sexes were obtained via in vitro fertilisation.
evidence: This describes the source and method of obtaining experimental subjects.

claim: Embryos were reared in 0.1× Modified Barth's Saline (MBS) at 14–18°C to reach the desired developmental stage.
source: Embryos were reared in 0.1× Modified Barth's Saline (MBS) at 14–18°C to reach the desired developmental stage, as described by Nieuwkoop and Faber, 1958.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol for embryo culture, with citation to established methods.

claim: All embryos used in this study were below stage 45.
source: All embryos used in this study were below stage 45.
evidence: This specifies the developmental stage range of experimental subjects.

claim: The ath5::GAP-eGFP construct consists of a membrane-tagged GFP fusion under control of the retinal ganglion cell (RGC)-specific atonal homolog 5 promoter.
source: The construct consisted of a membrane-tagged GFP fusion under control of the retinal ganglion cell (RGC)-specific atonal homolog 5 promoter (Kanekar et al., 1997).
evidence: This describes the composition of the genetic construct used, with citation.

claim: The ath5::GAP-eGFP construct selectively labelled RGCs in a single retina.
source: This selectively labelled RGCs in a single retina
evidence: This describes the specificity of the labeling achieved with the construct.

claim: RGC axons grew across the optic chiasm and into the unlabelled brain hemisphere.
source: the axons of which grew across the optic chiasm and into the unlabelled brain hemisphere
evidence: This describes the anatomical trajectory of labeled axons.

claim: Stage 33/34 embryos were anaesthetised for the exposed brain preparation.
source: Stage 33/34 embryos were anaesthetised
evidence: This describes a step in the experimental protocol.

claim: The eye primordium was removed to expose the underlying brain hemisphere.
source: the eye primordium was removed and the underlying brain hemisphere exposed as described (Chien et al., 1993; Irie et al., 2002)
evidence: This describes the surgical procedure used, with citations to established methods.

claim: Higher osmolarity retards skin regrowth, allowing for experiments spanning several hours.
source: The higher osmolarity retards skin regrowth, allowing for experiments spanning several hours.
evidence: This explains the rationale for using higher osmolarity medium.

claim: Embryo viability throughout all in vivo experiments was assessed by the presence of a visible heartbeat.
source: Embryo viability throughout all in vivo experiments was assessed by the presence of a visible heartbeat (which begins at st. 33/34 (Gurdon et al., 1997)).
evidence: This describes the method for assessing embryo viability, with citation.

claim: The heartbeat begins at stage 33/34 in Xenopus embryos.
source: which begins at st. 33/34 (Gurdon et al., 1997)
evidence: This is a developmental fact cited from the literature.

claim: Polyacrylamide hydrogels with 5% AA and 0.07% Bis-AA in PBS have a shear modulus of approximately 300 Pa.
source: a premix composition previously determined to give a shear modulus G (a measure of stiffness) of ~300 Pa (5% AA, 0.07% Bis-AA in PBS)
evidence: This describes the mechanical properties of a specific hydrogel formulation.

claim: Stiff gels comprised of 7.5% AA/0.2% Bis-AA in PBS have a shear modulus of approximately 5,500 Pa.
source: Stiff gels were comprised of 7.5% AA/0.2% Bis-AA in PBS, resulting in a shear modulus of G ~5,500 Pa
evidence: This describes the mechanical properties of stiff hydrogels used in experiments.

claim: Soft gels comprised of 5% AA/0.04% Bis-AA in PBS have a shear modulus of approximately 200 Pa.
source: soft gels were comprised of 5% AA/0.04% Bis-AA in PBS, resulting in G ~200 Pa
evidence: This describes the mechanical properties of soft hydrogels used in experiments.

claim: Eye primordia explants were cultured at 20°C for 22–24 hr in Xenopus cell culture medium.
source: Dishes were cultured at 20°C for 22–24 hr in Xenopus cell culture medium (60% L15 medium + 1× PSF, adjusted to pH 7.6–7.8, and filter sterilized).
evidence: This describes the culture conditions for in vitro experiments.

claim: The thermal noise method was used to calibrate tipless silicon cantilevers and determine the spring constant k.
source: Tipless silicon cantilevers (Arrow-TL1, NanoWorld) were calibrated using the thermal noise method (Hutter and Bechhoefer, 1993) to determine the spring constant k
evidence: This describes the calibration method with citation to the established technique.

claim: Cantilevers with spring constants between 0.02–0.04 N/m were selected for AFM measurements.
source: those with k between 0.02–0.04 N/m were selected
evidence: This describes the selection criteria for cantilevers.

claim: Monodisperse spherical polystyrene beads with diameter 37.28 ± 0.34 µm were glued to cantilever ends as probes.
source: Monodisperse spherical polystyrene beads (diameter 37.28 ± 0.34 µm; microParticles GmbH) were glued to the cantilever ends as probes.
evidence: This describes the AFM probe preparation with specific dimensions.

claim: AFM indentation measurements used a maximum indentation force of 10 nN.
source: Indentation measurements (maximum indentation force: 10 nN, approach speed: 5 µm/s, data rate: 1,000 Hz)
evidence: This describes the AFM measurement parameters.

claim: AFM indentation measurements used an approach speed of 5 µm/s.
source: Indentation measurements (maximum indentation force: 10 nN, approach speed: 5 µm/s, data rate: 1,000 Hz)
evidence: This describes the AFM measurement parameters.

claim: AFM indentation measurements used a data rate of 1,000 Hz.
source: Indentation measurements (maximum indentation force: 10 nN, approach speed: 5 µm/s, data rate: 1,000 Hz)
evidence: This describes the AFM measurement parameters.

claim: After each AFM measurement, the cantilever was retracted by 100 µm.
source: After each measurement, the cantilever was retracted by 100 µm
evidence: This describes the AFM measurement protocol.

claim: The stage moved by 20–25 µm between successive AFM measurement positions.
source: the stage moved by a set distance (20–25 µm) to the next position (Koser et al., 2016)
evidence: This describes the spatial resolution of AFM mapping with citation.

claim: Xenopus brains are optically opaque.
source: To allow simultaneous time-lapse imaging of the growing OT and in vivo stiffness measurements of live Xenopus brains, which are optically opaque
evidence: This is a statement about the optical properties of the tissue.

claim: An upright epifluorescence set-up was custom-fit above the AFM head to enable simultaneous optical imaging and AFM measurements.
source: an upright epifluorescence set-up was custom-fit above the AFM head
evidence: This describes the custom instrumentation developed for the study.

claim: The microscope was based on a Zeiss AxioZoom V16 fluorescence stereomicroscope without eyepieces.
source: which was based on a Zeiss AxioZoom V16 fluorescence stereomicroscope (without eyepieces)
evidence: This describes the optical components of the custom setup.

claim: A long working distance objective with automatic zoom and high NA allowed in vivo fluorescence imaging of RGC axons through the transparent AFM head.
source: A long working distance objective with automatic zoom and high NA (PlanApo Z 0.5×/0.125, working distance 114 mm, Zeiss) allowed in vivo fluorescence imaging of RGC axons through the transparent AFM head
evidence: This describes the optical capabilities of the custom setup.

claim: Stage 33/34 embryos with ath5::GAP-eGFP-labelled OTs in which the OT was clearly visible but had not yet formed the mid-OT bend were selected for tiv-AFM experiments.
source: Stage 33/34 embryos with ath5::GAP-eGFP-labelled OTs were prepared with one brain hemisphere exposed as described above, and those in which the OT was clearly visible (but had not yet formed the mid-OT bend) were selected.
evidence: This describes the selection criteria for experimental subjects.

claim: A measurement region of approximately 150 × 250 µm was defined to include both the growing OT and the region of the mid-diencephalic turn.
source: a measurement region of approximately 150 × 250 µm defined to include both the growing OT and the region of the mid-diencephalic turn
evidence: This describes the spatial extent of AFM measurements.

claim: A stiffness map was collected and iterated over the same area every approximately 35 minutes.
source: A stiffness map of the area was collected and the map iterated over the same area every ~35 min.
evidence: This describes the temporal resolution of time-lapse AFM measurements.

claim: At the end of every line in the measurement grid, a fluorescence image of the optic tract was automatically collected.
source: At the end of every line in the measurement grid, the stage was moved back to a pre-defined location and a fluorescence image of the optic tract automatically collected.
evidence: This describes the protocol for simultaneous imaging and AFM measurements.

claim: Temperature was maintained at 25°C for the duration of tiv-AFM measurements.
source: Temperature was maintained at 25°C for the duration of the measurement by a PetriDish Heater (JPK Instruments).
evidence: This describes the environmental control during experiments.

claim: Force-distance curves obtained from stiffness measurements were fitted to the Hertz model to obtain the reduced apparent elastic modulus K.
source: Force-distance curves obtained from stiffness measurements were analysed with a custom-written MATLAB script (Koser et al., 2016; Christ et al., 2010) to obtain the reduced apparent elastic modulus K. Raw AFM data were fitted to the Hertz model
evidence: This describes the data analysis method with citations.

claim: Force-distance curves were analysed at the maximum applied force F = 10 nN.
source: Force-distance curves were analysed at the maximum applied force F = 10 nN.
evidence: This describes the analysis parameters for AFM data.

claim: Force-distance curves were excluded if there was inability to apply linear fits through the baseline region due to noise.
source: criteria for excluding individual force-distance curves were (1) inability to apply linear fits through the baseline region, for example due to noise
evidence: This describes the quality control criteria for data analysis.

claim: Force-distance curves were excluded if there was inability to apply good-quality Hertzian fits to the indentation region.
source: (2) inability to apply good-quality Hertzian fits to the indentation region, that is, the fit did not align with the raw data
evidence: This describes the quality control criteria for data analysis.

claim: Previously sorted, gridded AFM data were smoothed in x-, y-, and time dimensions using an algorithm based on the discrete cosine transform.
source: previously sorted, gridded AFM data were smoothed in x-, y-, and time dimensions using an algorithm based on the discrete cosine transform by Garcia et al (Garcia, 2010; Garcia, 2011)
evidence: This describes the data processing method with citations.

claim: An iteratively weighted version of the penalized least squares approach was used to smooth the data and interpolate missing values.
source: an iteratively weighted version of the penalized least squares approach was used to smooth the data and interpolate missing values where the force-distance curves were not analysable
evidence: This describes the specific smoothing algorithm used.

claim: The smoothing algorithm uses the entire data set to interpolate missing values, as opposed to only the nearest neighbouring data.
source: This algorithm has the advantage of using the entire data set to interpolate missing values, as opposed to only the nearest neighbouring data (as, for example, in other smoothing methods such as a simple spline interpolation).
evidence: This explains the advantage of the chosen smoothing method.

claim: Local tissue stiffness gradients were calculated for a 50 × 50 µm² region of interest on the rostral and caudal sides of the OT.
source: Mean values of K were calculated for a 50 × 50 µm2 region of interest (ROI) on the rostral (KR) and caudal sides (KC) of the OT
evidence: This describes the method for quantifying stiffness gradients.

claim: For each frame in a time-lapse series, ROIs were defined three times and the mean of the three measurements was used for analysis.
source: For each frame in a given time-lapse series, ROIs were defined three times and the mean of the three measurements for each ROI was used for further analysis.
evidence: This describes the measurement replication protocol.

claim: The magnitude of the OT turn was calculated using the FIJI Angle tool by defining three points: chiasm, mid-diencephalic turn, and end of OT.
source: The magnitude of the OT turn was calculated from each frame of these movies using the FIJI Angle tool. Three points were defined manually (chiasm, mid-diencephalic turn, and end of OT) such that the two lines drawn through these points ran through the centre of the OT.
evidence: This describes the method for quantifying axon turning.

claim: Each OT turning angle measurement was repeated three times and averaged.
source: Each measurement was repeated three times, averaged
evidence: This describes the measurement replication protocol.

claim: A positive OT turning angle value denotes turning in the caudal direction.
source: a positive value denotes turning in the caudal direction
evidence: This defines the convention for interpreting turning angle measurements.

claim: Elongation of the OT was calculated by the major-to-minor axis ratio using an automated algorithm.
source: Elongation of the OT was calculated by the major-to-minor axis ratio using a previously described automated algorithm in Matlab (Koser et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the method for quantifying OT elongation with citation.

claim: Axes for OT elongation were determined by fitting ellipses with the same normalized second central moment as the OT area.
source: axes were determined by fitting ellipses, with the same normalized second central moment as the OT area, around the OTs
evidence: This describes the specific algorithm for calculating elongation.

claim: Two 50 μm × 50 μm regions of interest matching the size used in stiffness gradient analysis were selected rostral and caudal to the OT caudal bend for cell body density measurements.
source: Two 50 μm × 50 μm regions of interest (matching the size of regions of interest used in stiffness gradient analysis) were selected, rostral (DR) and caudal (DC) to the region corresponding to the OT caudal bend.
evidence: This describes the method for measuring cell body density in regions corresponding to stiffness measurements.

claim: Relative cell body density was calculated by dividing the area occupied by nuclei by the total region area.
source: Relative cell body density was calculated by dividing the area occupied by nuclei by the total region area.
evidence: This describes the calculation method for cell body density.

claim: Normalised brain areas were obtained by calculating the ratio of exposed brain area to intact brain area.
source: Normalised brain areas were obtained by calculating the ratio of exposed brain area to intact brain area.
evidence: This describes the normalization method for brain area measurements.

claim: pH3+ cells were counted and normalized to the total measured brain area in each section.
source: pH3+ cells were counted and normalized to the total measured brain area in each section
evidence: This describes the quantification method for mitotic cells.

claim: Data were collected from at least three independent experiments (N ≥ 3).
source: Data were collected from at least three independent experiments (N ≥ 3).
evidence: This describes the experimental replication standard.

claim: The order of data collection was randomized with no blinding.
source: The order of data collection was randomized with no blinding
evidence: This describes the experimental design regarding randomization and blinding.

claim: No data were excluded from the analysis.
source: no data were excluded from the analysis
evidence: This describes the data inclusion policy.

claim: Non-parametric tests and linear regression analysis were used for statistical analyses of the data.
source: Non-parametric tests as well as linear regression analysis were used for statistical analyses of the data as described in the figure captions.
evidence: This describes the statistical methods used.

claim: R² values provide an estimate of the quality of the fits used in the plots.
source: R2 values provide an estimate of the quality of the fits used in the plots.
evidence: This explains the interpretation of R² values.

claim: Pearson's correlation coefficient provides a measure of the magnitude of correlation between the cell body density gradient and the stiffness gradient.
source: Pearson's correlation coefficient, on the other hand, provides a measure of the magnitude of correlation between the cell body density gradient and the stiffness gradient.
evidence: This explains the use of Pearson's correlation coefficient in the analysis.
